soc: Snapdragon 7s Gen 2 (IN/global) / Snapdragon 6 Gen 1 (LATAM incl. BR)
notes: Regional SoC split: BR/LATAM units use Snapdragon 6 Gen 1, India/global use 7s Gen 2 (confirmed via spot-check). India launch May 2024 at Rs 22,999. Android 16 rollout confirmed. Still sold in BR; largely replaced by Edge 60/70 Fusion in IN.
caveats: Motorola historically hides aux camera IDs from third-party Camera2 apps despite native-app access (GameChanger); some newer Edge models report third-party success — runtime UW probe mandatory; advertised 120 deg is a comfortable FOV pass on paper. Both regional Snapdragons (7s Gen 2 / 6 Gen 1) are in the reliable Qualcomm encoder family. NOT on the ARCore certified list (while Edge 60 Fusion IS) — timestamp source unverified; absence could be page lag. QA should treat IN and BR units as two distinct SoC configs.

model_numbers: XT2403-2 (IN); BR variant in XT2403 series
notes: World-first SD 7 Gen 3 phone. India launch Apr 2024 at ~Rs 31,999; Brazil Apr 2024 at R$3,499. Among the first Motorolas to receive stable Android 16 (Sep 2025). Phased out in favor of Edge 60/70 Pro.
caveats: 120 deg UW is a comfortable FOV pass on paper, but Motorola third-party Camera2 access to the UW sub-camera is mixed-by-model — runtime probe (zoom-ratio lower bound <1.0 OR separate UW ID) required. Snapdragon 7 Gen 3 encoder family is reliable for HEVC CBR. NOT found on the ARCore certified list (snapshot 2026-06-12) — REALTIME timestamp source unverified despite upper-midrange class.

model_numbers: XT2401-2 (reported; GSMArena lists no Models line)
notes: India launch Jun 18, 2024 at Rs 59,999 (12/512, Flipkart); Brazil May 2024 at R$5,999 (suggested R$6,299). Android 16-eligible (Edge 50 family). Phased out as the Edge 70 Pro/Pro+ arrived.
caveats: Flagship-class hardware: 122 deg / 50 MP UW (comfortable FOV pass) and Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 (reliable encoder family). Blocked from Supported only by Motorola's mixed third-party UW exposure — runtime probe required. Surprisingly ABSENT from the ARCore certified list snapshot (older Edge 30 Ultra is listed) — timestamp 'likely' rests on the Snapdragon-flagship REALTIME pattern, not certification.

notes: India launch Sep 16, 2024 at Rs 23,999 (8/256, Flipkart + motorola.in); Brazil launch Sep/Oct 2024. Promised up to 5 OS upgrades; stable Android 16 arrived Mar 2026. Being replaced by Edge 60 Neo.
caveats: ARCore CERTIFIED (confirmed on Google's device list 2026-06-12) — strong signal for IMU rate + REALTIME timestamps. Main risk is the MediaTek Dimensity 7300 encoder: all MTK encoders ignore frame timestamps for rate control (WebRTC forces FRAMERATE_ADJUSTMENT) and the budget-Dimensity family has documented HEVC timestamp jitter — compat-check MUST verify isBitrateModeSupported(CBR) and stamp output. UW reachability needs the standard Motorola runtime probe.

notes: Vanilla Edge 50 (Aug 2024) — slimmest MIL-STD-810H + IP68 phone at launch. India Aug 2024 at ~Rs 27,999; Brazil Aug 2024 at R$2,999 (R$2,699 cash). 50MP main + 10MP 3x tele + 13MP UW. Android 16-eligible (up to 5 OS upgrades promised).
caveats: Snapdragon 7 Gen 1 AE is in the reliable Qualcomm encoder family. 120 deg UW comfortable on paper; Motorola third-party UW exposure mixed — runtime probe required. NOT on the ARCore certified list snapshot (sibling Edge 50 Neo IS) — timestamp source unverified.

model_numbers: XT2503-4 (per GSMArena; regional variants in XT2503 series)
notes: India launch Apr 2025 (Dimensity 7400 variant); Brazil launch May 2025 with the Edge 60 wave. Stable Android 16 received (Sep 2025 wave). Still on sale alongside Edge 70 Fusion. Regional SoC split confirmed via GSMArena.
caveats: ARCore CERTIFIED (confirmed 2026-06-12) — IMU + timestamp gates strongly supported. Encoder is the open risk: Dimensity 7300/7400 are mid-tier MediaTek — silent CBR-to-VBR fallback and timestamp-assumed rate control documented in the family; compat-check must require isBitrateModeSupported(CBR). UW reachability needs the Motorola runtime probe. IN (D7400) and BR (D7300) are distinct SoC configs for QA.

notes: Global/BR launch Apr 2025 (Dimensity 7300 per GSMArena); India launch Jun 10, 2025 (single 12/256, Dimensity 7400 — confirmed via Digit/Beebom, sale Jun 17 via Flipkart). 50MP ultrawide — GSMArena lists 122 deg, much marketing copy says 120 deg (either is a comfortable pass). Stable Android 16 received.
caveats: Three stacked unknowns: (1) mid-tier MediaTek encoder (D7300/7400) — CBR honoring unverified, family has documented timestamp-assumed rate control; (2) NOT on the ARCore certified list snapshot even though siblings Edge 60 Fusion/Stylus are — REALTIME timestamp unverified (absence may be page lag); (3) Motorola third-party UW exposure mixed — runtime probe required. FOV source disagreement (GSMArena 122 vs marketing 120) is immaterial — both pass comfortably.

model_numbers: XT2601-2 (global; IN + BR variants in XT2601 series)
price_inr: Rs 29,999 (launch Dec 2025; effective Rs 28,999 with offers)
notes: 5.99mm ultra-thin flagship-lite; global version of China's Moto X70 Air. Global release Oct 29, 2025; India Dec 15, 2025 (single 8/256); Brazil Mar 2026. Ships on Android 16, 3–4 OS upgrades promised (region-dependent).
caveats: THERMAL is the headline risk: 5.99mm chassis — reviews measured ~50 C surface temps during 20-min 4K recording/gaming sessions, GPU throttles to ~64% after 20 min, noticeable throttling around 30 min (Smartprix/PhoneArena/GSMArena). 1080p30 HEVC is a lighter load and CPU held ~86-88% under stress, but the 25-min sustained-capture gate is unproven in this body — needs on-device thermal soak before any promotion. Encoder (SD 7 Gen 4) reliable. NOT on ARCore list snapshot (recent release, likely lag) — timestamp unverified. Motorola UW runtime probe required.
